title: Inaccurate loading bar in web export with GDExtension enabled
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable.arch_linux

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable unknown - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun, 11 Jan 2026 17:10:53 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (radeonsi, navi21, LLVM 21.1.6, DRM 3.64, 6.18.5-arch1-1) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.26 GiB memory

### Issue description

When I open the game in a browser, the loading bar fills up very fast (even when simulating a relatively slow connection), and then stays there for as long as it takes to download ~41MB (the engine, I imagine) of `index.side.html`, as well as any GDExtension wasm files.

The wait also includes some engine startup which takes maybe half a second, which is annoying for local testing (loading bar fills up instantly, then stays there for half a second, and then the initial scene opens), but probably a pretty marginal issue when actually having to download the engine with a limited download speed.

Ideally the loading bar would either fill up so that it only reaches 100% right before opening the initial scene, or at the very least show an "indeterminate" animation if it can't estimate progress, instead of showing 100% for most of the loading time (/vast majority of the loading time on a slow connection).

### Steps to reproduce

Make a web export of a game with "Extension support" enabled and open the exported game in a browser.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24649675/mrp.zip)
